subject: Post-call: Multilingual evals & recommended models — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hoffman <lena.hoffman@globexretail.com>, procurement@globexretail.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Multilingual evals & recommended models — next steps

Hi Lena,

Thanks again for a great conversation earlier — appreciated the context on Globex Retail's multilingual customer support pilot. Quick recap and next steps below.

Key takeaways:
- Pilot scope: automated triage + locale-aware canned responses for EU languages (DE, FR, ES) and APAC (JA, KO).
- Volume estimate: 1.2M messages/month for pilot region set; peak latency target < 350ms for canned responses.
- Quality bar: precision-like metric target 92% on intent classification and 88% on response appropriateness in localized QA.
- Data constraints: cannot send PII outside EU for EU traffic; will need Private deployment or regional routing.

Recommendations I promised after the call:
1) Model shortlist for evaluation: open-llama-3-8b-multilingual for cheap baseline; redwood-instruct-v2-13b for higher-quality generation; xglm-7b-multilingual as another candidate.
2) Eval assets: prompt_set_eu_apac.jsonl (attached) with locale-specific prompt templates and golden responses; initial benchmark workbook globex_multilingual_eval_v1.xlsx (attached) with per-locale pass/fail thresholds.
3) Monitoring / regression guardrails: set up prompt-based regression tests (nightly) + per-locale quality dashboards. We can run a 2-week A/B eval across 50k samples per locale.

Next steps / asks:
- Lena: confirm preferred EU locales and whether Globex can share a 5k-sample masked dataset for initial runs (PII redacted).
- Procurement: I'll loop Neha for pricing ballpark and contract options (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
- Rishi / Dev: can you prepare a short canary rollout plan and estimated infra for the 50k-sample evaluation?

I attached the evaluation workbook and prompt set and included a Drive link with raw prompts and a benchmarking script.

Proposed follow-up: 30 minute results sync on Thu 2027-03-11 10:00 CET (9:00 GMT). If that works I will send an invite.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: globex_multilingual_eval_v1.xlsx, prompt_set_eu_apac.jsonl, redwood_recommendations_v2.pdf

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap and the assets — really helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we schedule the follow-up: 

1) For EU locales we definitely want DE, FR, ES to be prioritized. We may add NL and IT later but not for the initial run.
2) For APAC, Japanese and Korean are highest priority; Chinese will be out of scope for now.
3) On the quality thresholds: the 92% / 88% targets are fine as goals, but procurement will want a concrete SLA we can commit to for latency and availability.

Also two technical Qs for Rishi / your team: 
- Do you have language-specific tokenization/segmentation recommendations? We observed higher hallucination rates on polite-form Japanese prompts in prior tests.
- For regression monitoring, what does the nightly test look like (pass/fail, delta thresholds)? We need to know how we get alerted if a model update causes a >3% drop in appropriateness per locale.

Procurement: we'll need a ballpark price range for hosted vs dedicated vs private, even just order-of-magnitude, to prepare our internal ask.

Can we move the sync to Thu 2027-03-11 at 10:30 CET?

Thanks,
Lena
Head of Digital CX, Globex Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hoffman <lena.hoffman@globexretail.com>, procurement@globexretail.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-10T19:10:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Multilingual evals & recommended models — next steps

Lena — great, thanks for confirming the locale set. Answers inline below and attachments updated in Drive.

Locale recommendations:
- EU: DE/FR/ES as priority. We'll run separate prompt templates per locale in prompt_set_eu_apac.jsonl.
- APAC: JA/KO prioritized. For Japanese polite-form, we recommend explicit persona anchors in the prompt and a shorter decoding top-p to reduce verbosity.

Tokenization / segmentation:
- For JA/KO we recommend using SentencePiece models trained with subword vocab that includes common honorifics; this reduces token fragmentation that can lead to hallucinations. Our eval script includes a tokenizer config in the Drive folder.

Regression monitoring approach:
- Nightly regression run: run 2k locale-specific test items through current production candidate and baseline. Compute delta on the appropriateness score and precision. Alerting: >2% drop triggers an automated pager to the SRE/MLOps on-call; >3% opens an incident with rollback flag. We can tune thresholds per-locale.

Model shortlist and expected tradeoffs:
- open-llama-3-8b-multilingual: cheapest, good for intent classification; lower generation fidelity in long-form localized responses.
- xglm-7b-multilingual: strong cross-lingual intent + reasonable generation quality.
- redwood-instruct-v2-13b: highest quality for canned responses and nuance; higher cost and memory.

I've uploaded updated benchmark sheets to the Drive and attached globex_multilingual_eval_v1.xlsx and prompt_set_eu_apac.jsonl to this thread. Neha, can you drop a pricing ballpark for hosted vs dedicated vs private? Dev/ Rishi: can you share a short canary rollout plan in the Drive folder by end of day tomorrow?

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: globex_multilingual_eval_v1.xlsx, prompt_set_eu_apac.jsonl

Quick pricing note for planning (ballpark figures, subject to final SOW):
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): $0.12 - $0.25 per 1k generated tokens depending on model; embeddings/intent classification priced separately.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): starting around $12k/month for a small reserved pool with predictable throughput; scales with GPU type and commit.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): one-time platform fee + monthly support; typically starts ~$80k setup + $10k/mo for small deployments.

I'll prepare a short pricing options doc and put it in the Drive folder today. For procurement planning, we can include an SLA appendix showing latency and availability targets for Dedicated/Private.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
